---
title: Publishing
description: Getting a plugin to users. Remote plugins are listed in the marketplace registry. Bundled plugins are merged into pku-harness-plugins and reach phones as a signed OTA update or with the next app release.
icon: Send
---

## Remote plugins

1. Deploy your MCP server over HTTPS ([Quickstart](/en/docs/build/remote-plugin#4-deploy)).
2. Make sure your MCP server `name` matches the registry `id` you'll use.
3. List it in the marketplace. Either add a manifest to your repository and submit it on this
   website ([manifest reference](/en/docs/marketplace/manifest), [submitting](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing)),
   or open a pull request that adds an entry to `registry/registry.json` in
   [`pku-harness-plugins`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins). Review and the
   `verified` badge are covered in the [review policy](/en/docs/marketplace/review).
4. Users install it from Settings → Plugins → Marketplace, or add your URL by hand.

Updates go out as soon as you deploy: the app picks up the new tool list the next time it refreshes
the plugin. Keep tool names stable. Renaming a tool breaks users' widgets and scheduled checks that
reference it.

## Bundled plugins

1. Open an issue in `pku-harness-plugins` first, saying what the plugin does and why it has to be
   bundled.
2. Send a pull request with `plugins/<id>/`, the `builtinPlugins` entry in `plugins/index.ts` and a
   `"kind": "builtin"` registry entry.
3. CI and reviewers run:

   ```bash
   bun test
   bunx tsc --noEmit -p .
   bun scripts/validate-registry.ts
   ```

4. After the merge, the app bumps its `plugins/` submodule to the new commit. JS-only changes reach
   phones as a signed over-the-air (OTA) update, applied on the next launch. Anything that needs
   native code waits for the next app release (a new APK).

Nothing is published to npm. The SDK and plugins are consumed straight from the GitHub repository.

## Renaming or merging

Never reuse or silently rename ids that users may have stored in widgets, checks or settings. Use
`PluginDef.legacy` to map old plugin ids, tool ids and widget keys to the new ones
([SDK → plugin](/en/docs/sdk/plugin#pluginlegacy)).

## Using PKU Harness Cloud

If the plugin declares `PluginDef.cloud`, copy its `cloud` declaration (`uses`, `e2e`,
`disclosure`, optional `backend`) into the registry entry. The marketplace shows it before
install, and `disclosure.zh` must say in plain words what leaves the device. See
[Cloud → plugin guide](/en/docs/cloud/plugin-guide#6-registry-entry).
